definitions.explanation: A type of collar that stands upright and fits close to the neck, or the uniform featuring such a collar. In Japan, typically refers to the traditional boys' school uniform (gakuran) with its stiff, buttoned-up standing collar.

examples.japanese: {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}の{学生服|がくせいふく}を{着|き}る。
examples.english: To wear a stand-up collar school uniform.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}が{中学|ちゅうがく}に{入|はい}るので、{詰|つ}め{襟|えり}を{買|か}いに{行|い}った。
examples.english: My son is entering middle school, so I went to buy a stand-up collar uniform.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}はブレザーの{学校|がっこう}が{増|ふ}えて、{詰|つ}め{襟|えり}の{制服|せいふく}は{少|すく}なくなってきた。
examples.english: Recently, more schools have adopted blazers, and stand-up collar uniforms have become less common.

notes:
CULTURE:
The {詰|つ}め{襟|えり} is iconic of Japanese boys' school uniforms, known as {学|がく}ラン. The design was originally inspired by European military uniforms and became standard in Japanese schools during the Meiji era. While many schools have switched to blazers, the {詰|つ}め{襟|えり} remains a recognized symbol of male student life in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}の{制服|せいふく} (stand-up collar uniform)
- {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}の{学生服|がくせいふく} (stand-up collar school uniform)
- {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}を{着|き}る (to wear a stand-up collar uniform)

ETYMOLOGY:
From {詰|つ}める (to pack tightly, to close up) + {襟|えり} (collar) — a collar that is closed up tightly around the neck.
